verdict.rationale: Parahelp's Customer Agent guardrails document topic-based routing to humans: a ticket about a given subject (enterprise accounts) is transferred to a team with a summary note. Separately, any tool can be gated behind Slack human approval, so sensitive actions cannot run on their own. Simulations let you check how the agent handles scenarios before release, but the evidence shows only a single routing example and no hard guarantee that the agent never responds on flagged topics. Missing for 10: explicit human-only topic designation (e.g. legal threats, cancellations, security), documented enforcement that the agent never replies on those topics, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a support ops lead, I mark topics as human-only — legal threats, cancellations, security — and the agent never freelances on them

citations.quote: When a ticket is about an enterprise account, transfer it to the enterprise team with a summary note.
Any tool can be gated behind human approval. Gated actions are sent to Slack with approve and deny buttons, and nothing runs until someone on your team approves.
